Build a pseudo-spectra MGF from one mzML file

Source: R/api.R
process_mzml.Rd

Single-sample route with no prior feature list. Steps:

Usage

process_mzml(
  path,
  tmp_dir,
  output = NULL,
  rt_range = c(30, 1200),
  grouper = NULL,
  group_statistics_fn = NULL,
  filter_fn = NULL
)

Arguments

path

mzML file path.

tmp_dir

Directory for the intermediate parquets.

output

MGF path. Required: the function stops before reading any data if it is NULL.

rt_range

Retention-time window (seconds) to keep.

grouper

A grouper closure (see grouper-contract); NULL uses ppm_upgma(ppm = 30).

group_statistics_fn

A statistics closure (see stats-contract); NULL uses correlation_statistics(min_count = 10).

filter_fn

A filter closure (see filter-contract); NULL uses correlation_filtering(cor_thresh = 0.1, fdr_thresh = 0.1).

Value

The clean_pseudo_spectra() table. The MGF is written as a side effect.

Details

  1. Read the file and keep spectra inside rt_range.

  2. If no spectrum is labelled MS2, assign MS levels by scan-index parity (bbCID alternates MS1/MS2). Aborts if the split is badly unbalanced.

  3. Detect chromatographic peaks with centWave (fixed parameters: peakwidth = c(2, 30), snthresh = 6, ppm = 12, prefilter = c(3, 1000), mzdiff = 0.01).

  4. Write pool/pointer parquets to tmp_dir and build one pseudo-spectrum per peak with clean_pseudo_spectra().

  5. Write the MGF with export_mgf().

See also

Other api: carpediams(), process_targetlist(), process_xcms()
